title: Descartes decision map
description: Analysis decisions recorded as reviewable cards, kept next to the code. Format version 0.1.

agent.description: The coding agent that works on the analysis, e.g. "Claude Code".

root.description: Folder that code paths are relative to, relative to the map file. Defaults to the map's folder.

changelog.description: Markdown file, relative to the map file, whose entries mention decisions as [decision-id].

stages.description: Pipeline stages in order. When present, every decision's stage must be one of these ids.

papers.description: Paper maps (decision maps of published analyses), relative to this file.

paper.description: Present only in a paper map: the paper whose analysis the map records.

notebook.description: Notebook or script that implements the stage.

question.description: The choice, as a short noun phrase.

status.description: decided: exactly one option is chosen. open: waiting for a person; no option is chosen.

risk.description: How much the result could change if this decision is wrong.

depends_on.description: Ids of earlier decisions this one depends on.

code.description: Lines of code that implement the chosen option.

notebook.description: Notebook or script where the decision is made.

matches.description: Paper maps only: ids of decisions in the main map that ask the same question.

value.description: The option, e.g. "0.1 Hz high-pass" or 0.1.

state.description: chosen: used. tested: run and compared, not used. rejected: ruled out. untried: considered, not run.

evidence.description: Numbers behind the option, each with its measure and unit.

lines.description: First and last line, 1-based and inclusive. In a Jupyter notebook, lines are counted over its code cells only.

sha256.description: Hash of the linked lines when a person last reviewed them. Absent means not reviewed yet.

expect.description: The linked line as a person reads it. For orientation only; check compares sha256.

pdf.description: PDF of the paper, relative to the map.

stages.description: own: the paper's own steps. main: the stages of the main map.

reader.description: Who filled the map, e.g. an AI model or a person.
